ledger.claim: The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is not met. The clause requires BOTH at least one in-app chat message AND at least one in-app call before trip_record.cancelled_at. The trip record's in_app_calls list is empty (derived contact_before_cancel.call_count = 0, calls: []) and the chat log contains three IN_APP text messages and no voice-call entry, so the call limb is absent. On that failure the clause voids the fee: the 5.00 SGD cancellation charge must be reversed and the rider is not charged.

The messaging limb alone cannot satisfy POL-NS-23. The derived contact_before_cancel block records message_count 3 at 08:52:10, 08:55:20 and 08:57:40 — all before the 08:58:30 cancellation — yet obligation_met is false precisely because call_count is 0. A message-only approach falls short of the two-limb test, and the driver's own statement ('Messaged 3 times. Passenger slow.') asserts no call at all, so the driver does not even claim to have met it.

The money follows the void. The payments ledger shows cancellation_fee 5.00 SGD, total_charged 5.00 SGD, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so the whole contested amount is still outstanding on the rider's payment method. Voiding the fee under POL-NS-23 returns the full 5.00 SGD — FULL_REFUND as POL-GEN-03 defines it, the filing party entirely right and the whole contested amount returned — and leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge.

POL-NS-23 attaches a specific consequence to the failure: the fee is voided 'with no driver compensation'. The ruling should therefore be FULL_REFUND with amount_sgd 5.00 and driver_compensation_sgd null, not DRIVER_COMPENSATION; the fee does not transfer to the driver (POL-GEN-03: driver_compensation_sgd carries money the ruling moves). The driver is not out of pocket on a ruling that reverses a charge the clause says should never have been levied.

This ruling can be issued by the AI rather than escalated. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts — the trip record and the chat log — is COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes, so the 0.95 confidence POL-GEN-22 requires (a party's profile carries a fraud flag) is attainable from clean, mutually corroborating evidence: the empty in_app_calls list and the message-only chat log agree. Because the contact facts ARE established by the record, POL-GEN-26 is not engaged — there is no fact the record cannot establish.

ledger.claim: The driver reached the pickup as POL-NS-21 contemplates: the trip record's arrival event at 08:51:50 is corroborated by the driver-device trace, whose nearest fix sits 5.04 m from the pickup point - far inside the 50 m arrival radius for the STANDARD pickup zone - and the derived arrival_check reports corroborated = true. The trace is COMPLETE, at 100% coverage with no gap above 30 s, so the arrival fact rests on clean evidence at full weight.

On an on-demand trip POL-NS-21's free wait runs from the driver's arrival. The driver stood at the pickup from 08:51:50 until cancellation at 08:58:30 - 400 s, which is 100 s beyond the 300 s free wait that expired at 08:56:50 - so the cancellation was made after the free wait and POL-NS-22's timing condition for a chargeable no-show is satisfied.

The amount charged is the policy amount: the payments ledger carries a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, charged at 08:58:34, and the derived money block reports fee_matches_policy = true against POL-NS-22's 5.00 SGD no-show fee. The fee charged is therefore the fee POL-NS-22 transfers to the driver as compensation for time and fuel where it stands.

The rider had actual notice and did not board. The arrival push went at 08:51:54, and all three driver messages were delivered and read before the 08:58:30 cancellation (read receipts 08:52:35, 08:55:45, 08:57:53). The rider's own claim - 'I was coming down with my kids' - attributes the delay to the rider, so the wait POL-NS-22 compensates was time and fuel lost to a genuine no-show rather than to any default of the driver's.

POL-NS-24's additional 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not arise. That limb is conditioned on the driver having 'also failed to attempt contact', and this driver attempted contact three times in-app before cancelling; the record also shows the trip was cancelled_by DRIVER, so the no-charge cancellation right POL-NS-24 addresses - a rider's cancellation after a driver no-show - was never exercised.

The driver's profile carries fraud_flags = 1. POL-GEN-22 uses that field only to raise the confidence an AI ruling needs on this 5.00 SGD dispute to 0.95, and POL-GEN-01 is explicit that it never decides a trip. It is therefore not evidence about this trip, and the arrival, wait and notice facts above rest on independent platform telemetry, not on any profile field.

Concession, on the record as it stands: POL-NS-23's contact obligation is not met on the driver's side. trip_record.in_app_calls is empty and the chat log contains no voice-call entry, so the driver messaged but placed no in-app call before cancelling, and the driver's own statement ('Messaged 3 times') does not assert one. On POL-NS-23 the fee is voided and the rider is not charged, with no driver compensation - the rider's claim on that point is supported, and the fee cannot survive it.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee charged to your payment method at 08:58:34 is reversed in full (FULL_REFUND, amount_sgd 5.00, driver_compensation_sgd null). POL-NS-23 says a driver cancelling for no-show must first BOTH send an in-app chat message AND place an in-app call before cancellation (trip_record.cancelled_at = 08:58:30). The record shows the messaging limb met — three INS-APP driver messages at 08:52:10, 08:55:20 and 08:57:40, all read (08:52:35, 08:55:45, 08:57:53) before the cancellation — but the call limb is absent: trip_record.in_app_calls is empty (derived contact_before_cancel.call_count = 0) and the chat log contains no voice-call entry. Because one of the two required limbs is missing, POL-NS-23 voids the fee; the whole contested 5.00 SGD is returned to you and no compensation is transferred to the driver. The missing third-party traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-06064-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact and changes nothing: the fee falls on the contact obligation, not on any question of traffic. To the driver: your arrival at 08:51:50 was corroborated by the driver-device trace (nearest fix 5.04 m from the pickup, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius; arrival_check.corroborated = true), and POL-NS-21's free wait — which on this on-demand trip runs from your arrival — expired at 08:56:50, so your 08:58:30 cancellation came after the 300 s wait, satisfying POL-NS-22's timing condition, and the 5.00 SGD charged matches the policy fee (fee_matches_policy = true). The rider was also notified (arrival push 08:51:54) and read all three messages. None of that rescues the fee, because POL-NS-23's two-limb contact test is conjunctive and the call was never made. For the same reason there is no POL-NS-24 goodwill credit: you did attempt contact, and there was no driver no-show, so that limb never fires; and the driver's own statement ('Messaged 3 times') concedes that only messages were sent. On the figures: fee charged 5.00 SGD (EV-FARE-06064), refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so the full 5.00 SGD is outstanding and is returned. Confidence is 0.95: the driver's profile carries fraud_flags = 1, which under POL-GEN-22 raises the required confidence to 0.95 on this 5.00 SGD dispute (POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling final subject to that bar). That bar is attainable because the deciding fact rests on complete, full-weight artifacts — the platform trip record and the platform chat log, both status COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 — so the cap under POL-GEN-02(2) is 1.0. The fraud flag is used only as POL-GEN-01 and POL-GEN-22 permit, to set the confidence bar; it does not decide the trip, and no other profile field is relied on. POL-GEN-26 is not engaged: the facts the rule needs — whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling, and when the driver arrived — are established by the record. No clause in this policy produces a referral on these facts (the fee is exactly 5.00 SGD, so POL-NS-22's amount check does not fire; POL-NS-24's credit does not arise; POL-NS-25's counter, no_show_cancellations_30d, is absent from the rider profile).

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
